newsitem.title: UK: Copper price to fall in 1997, stocks rising - EIU.
newsitem.headline: Copper price to fall in 1997, stocks rising - EIU.

text.p: Copper prices will weaken further during the final part of this year and the trend will continue in 1997 as inventories increase, the Economist Intelligence Unit (EIU) said.
In its latest edition of world commodity forecasts the EIU said Western stocks will begin to rise in 1997, which will further depress prices.
"By 1998, stocks should have returned to their late 1993 peak, pushing prices below $0.75/lb," the EIU said.
Elsewhere, aluminium prices are currently undervalued, but will stay around $1,500/1,550 a tonne until early 1998 when an increase in demand will lead to some recovery in prices.
Higher lead prices are in prospect for 1997, with the market in deficit. But by 1998 the market will be in decline as supply catches up with demand, the EIU said.
In nickel, consumption has been affected by production cuts at European stainless steel mills, which will undermine prices in the medium term.
"Higher nickel production in 1998 will further depress an already weak market," the EIU said.
There will be significant price gains in tin in 1997 as recovering demand takes effect, while the zinc outlook is bullish with the market likely to be in deficit, it said.
